title: How skyscrapers stand tall
examples: How do buildings stay up when they are so high?
What keeps skyscrapers from falling over?
Does the wind push on tall buildings?

explain.say: Today we learn how very tall buildings stay up.
First we look at the steel frame inside the building.
The foundation spreads the building's weight deep into the ground.
Next we consider the force of the wind pushing on the sides.
Engineers use special shapes to let wind pass through easily.
In real life, think about a bridge crossing a river.

faq.q: Why do skyscrapers sway in the wind?
faq.a: They sway because wind pushes on them, and they are very tall. Engineers design them to move slightly instead of breaking.
asks: How much do tall buildings move?
Is it normal for skyscrapers to sway?

faq.q: Are steel frames always used in skyscrapers?
faq.a: No, other materials like reinforced concrete are also used. Engineers choose materials based on the design needs and location.
asks: Can buildings be made without steel?
Is concrete good enough for skyscrapers?

faq.q: How deep must the foundation go?
faq.a: The foundation must go deep enough to reach solid, stable soil or rock. This prevents the building from sinking unevenly.
asks: Does the foundation need to be very deep?
What does the foundation rest on?
How do they stop sinking into mud?

faq.q: What is aerodynamics in building design?
faq.a: Aerodynamics is the study of how air moves around objects. Architects use this to make buildings cut through the wind smoothly.
asks: How does air affect building shape?
Is air movement important for tall buildings?

faq.q: Do taller buildings need stronger foundations?
faq.a: Yes, generally, the taller the building, the greater the weight and the more force it must resist. This requires a much more robust foundation.
asks: Is weight related to foundation size?

facts: Steel frames provide the main skeleton for many skyscrapers.
Foundations must distribute the building's massive weight safely.
Wind exerts lateral (sideways) forces on tall structures.
Curved or tapered shapes reduce wind resistance effectively.

quiz.say: Which element primarily provides the internal skeleton for a skyscraper?
quiz.why: Steel frames create a rigid internal structure that supports floors and walls.

wrong.0: Beams are just one part; the whole frame is needed for support.
wrong.2: The foundation supports the building from below, not internally.
wrong.3: Wind is a force that the building must resist, not a support element.

quiz.say: If a building is built on soft mud, what part needs to be stronger?
quiz.why: The foundation must reach stable ground to prevent sinking into soft soil.

wrong.0: Wind resistance deals with side forces, not sinking into the ground.
wrong.1: Shape helps with wind, but the foundation handles the ground support.
wrong.3: The steel frame is strong, but it cannot fix weak ground underneath.

quiz.say: When designing for wind, which shape is generally better?
quiz.why: Curved shapes allow wind to flow around them smoothly, reducing pushing force.

wrong.0: Square shapes catch the wind head-on, causing more drag.
wrong.1: Thick walls help, but the overall shape is more important for wind flow.
wrong.2: Foundations stop sinking, but they do not stop wind pushing sideways.
